definitions.explanation: Describes something that is unclean or unkempt in an understated, casual way. The 小～ prefix softens the directness of 汚い, but the word still carries a negative nuance.

examples.japanese: {小汚|こぎたな}い⟦{格好|かっこう}→格好：01800_kakkou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{出|で}かけないで→出かける：00833_dekakeru⟧。

⟦{駅|えき}→駅：02180_eki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{裏|うら}→裏：02178_ura⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{小汚|こぎたな}い⟦{居酒屋|いざかや}→居酒屋：09635_izakaya⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦うまい→うまい：01279_umai⟧。
examples.english: There's a grubby izakaya behind the station, but the food is good.

examples.japanese: {小汚|こぎたな}い⟦アパート→アパート：01012_apaato⟧だった⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{住|す}んで→住む：00673_sumu⟧みる⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{居心地|いごこち}→居心地：06634_igokochi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦よかった→いい：00118_ii⟧。
examples.english: The apartment was dingy, but once I moved in, it was quite comfortable.

notes:
FORMS:
Uses the ⟦{小|こ}→小〜：00240_ko⟧～ prefix, which adds a sense of "somewhat" or "a little" to adjectives: {小暗|こぐら}い (dimly lit), {小寒|こざむ}い (slightly chilly). Despite the softening prefix, {小汚|こぎたな}い is still clearly negative.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {小汚|こぎたな}い⟦{格好|かっこう}→格好：01800_kakkou⟧ (scruffy appearance)
- {小汚|こぎたな}い⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧ (a dingy shop)
- {小汚|こぎたな}い⟦{路地|ろじ}→路地：06501_roji⟧ (a grubby alley)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{汚|きたな}い→汚い：00788_kitanai⟧: dirty — stronger and more direct
- ⟦むさ{苦|くる}しい→むさ苦しい：29821_musakurushii⟧: slovenly, unkempt — focuses on personal appearance
- ⟦みすぼらしい→みすぼらしい：07672_misuborashii⟧: shabby — emphasizes looking poor or worn out
